hypothesis: On a cold start the baseline downloads the 1,981 MiB Q8_0 GGUF into a memfd (25.0 s p50) and only then lets llama.cpp load it (model_load_mmap 8.4 s p50, which includes KleidiAI repacking each Q8_0 matmul weight as it reads it). The loader reads the header first and then each tensor once, so the load can start as soon as the header is present and repack each tensor as its bytes land. Overlapping the two should cut cold download+load from ~33.4 s towards max(download, load) plus the tail of the last tensors, and change no output. It cannot change a SnapStart restore, which never downloads or loads.

changed_variable.name: download/load overlap
changed_variable.baseline: download_to_memfd completes, then llama_model_load_from_file mmaps the memfd (P1)
changed_variable.experiment: llama_model_load_from_file starts once the GGUF header is in the memfd; a dormant llama.cpp hook (e4_stream/patch_stream.py) blocks each tensor's read until its bytes have arrived and loads tensors in expected-arrival order (arm stream). Same file, same download (HEAD + 31 x 64 MiB ranges on 32 threads), same mmap path and kernels. Arm streamfile keeps llama.cpp's own tensor order as a control

conclusion: Run 1 of 2 (arms base / stream / streamfile, 5 rounds x 10, interleaved; 0 errors; 1,800 of 1,800 answers bit-identical to P1's reference). Cold: stream cuts first-request time by 4.97 s pooled within CPU part (35.91 -> 31.44 s p50, -14 %; Graviton2 0xd0c -9.4 s, -19 %); download+load 33.72 -> 29.19 s p50; the download itself is unchanged (24.99 vs 24.99 s), the loader spends 18.7 s of it blocked on bytes. streamfile (llama.cpp's own order) cuts only 1.10 s: the order is what makes the overlap pay. Restore: SnapStart already hides the download and load (both run in publish_version's snapshot init, never in a restore), and stream makes restore WORSE: +0.41 s first-request (3.96 -> 4.35 s p50, +10 %; per-round medians do not overlap) because it uses +470 MB (Max Memory Used 5,160 -> 5,631 MB p50) on cold, restore and warm alike, and the larger snapshot takes longer to restore. Local diagnosis (same zip, real S3, malloc_stats): the extra is glibc thread-arena retention, about 16.7 MiB in each of the 32 download threads' arenas, because the overlapped KleidiAI repack frees large blocks while the download still allocates 8 MiB bodies, raising glibc's dynamic mmap threshold; malloc_trim returns only ~90 MB of it. Run 2 pins the threshold (mallopt M_MMAP_THRESHOLD = 4 MiB; locally: stream peak RSS 4.94 GB vs base 5.00 GB, answers identical) and measures the pin alone on base.
